blocks.text: The heading names Solomon, while the received book also contains distinct Solomonic collections, sayings from unnamed wise teachers, material copied by Hezekiah’s officials, words of Agur, and instruction from Lemuel’s mother. In this opening chapter, the stated purpose is educational: wisdom, discipline, justice, discernment, and the fear of Jehovah belong together as the beginning of knowledge. Wisdom is then portrayed as a woman calling publicly in the city. Across Proverbs 1–9, Wisdom and Folly are presented as rival female figures whose calls, paths, and invitations embody competing desires that lead toward life or death.

sections.title: Reading the Heading and Wisdom’s Voice
